writeup.headline: Inter & Co rates Hold: strong growth and quality are offset by a severe share-price downtrend.
writeup.thesis: Inter & Co scores 54, a Hold, because solid fundamentals are pulled down by very weak price action. Growth scores 77, with TTM revenue growth of 34.7% and growth sped up by 1.3 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores 75 on a 97.8% gross margin and a 57.5% FCF margin, though the diluted share count up 13.7% year on year weighs on it. Trend scores 0: the price is 59.8% below its 52-week high, 39.8% below its 200-day average, and shares are 54.2 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, with Lula's election win hitting Brazilian fintechs broadly. News risk is neutral at 50, and the balance sheet and valuation could not be scored, so the rating rests on growth, quality, trend and news alone.
key_risks: Political uncertainty in Brazil after Lula's election win, which hit Brazilian fintechs broadly
Deep price downtrend, with the price 30.1% below its 50-day average and 59.8% below its 52-week high
Shareholder dilution, with the diluted share count up 13.7% year on year
Q3 results expected around 2026-11-12 could disappoint after a period of fast growth
A senior leadership reshuffle adds execution uncertainty
what_would_change: An upgrade to Buy needs 11 more points, most plausibly from a recovery in the trend score from 0 as the price stabilises against its moving averages
A downgrade to Sell would follow a 10-point drop, for example if growth or quality scores weaken in the Q3 results
Positive news such as confirmed analyst upgrades or clearer Brazilian policy could lift the news risk score above 50, while further political pressure could push it lower
Scoring the balance sheet and valuation factors could move the composite either way
